stem: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of a normal thymus on a pediatric chest X-ray?

options.text: It often causes a significant mass effect on the trachea.
It has a uniform soft tissue density and sharply demarcated borders.
It is typically only visible in children older than 5 years.
It always appears symmetrical on both sides of the mediastinum.

explanation: The lecture defines a normal thymus as having uniform density and clear borders, often appearing triangular or scalloped.
rationale: Recall the 'sail sign' and its impact on neighboring airways.

optionExplanations.A: A key diagnostic feature of a normal thymus is that it never exerts mass effect on adjacent structures like the trachea.
optionExplanations.B: The lecture defines a normal thymus as having uniform density and clear borders, often appearing triangular or scalloped.
optionExplanations.C: The thymus is usually diminished or not visible on X-rays beyond the age of 2 or 3 years.
optionExplanations.D: The material mentions that the thymus is often quite asymmetrical, sometimes appearing only on one side.

originalCorrectOptionTexts: It has a uniform soft tissue density and sharply demarcated borders.
